title: Acceptable sources for risk adjustment
question: Can this document support a diagnosis code for risk adjustment? Assign the code it supports, or 'no code' if it cannot be used.
note:
Chief Complaint
COPD follow-up.

HPI
Pt is a 75-year-old female presenting for a face-to-face office visit for management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Pt reports she has been feeling well since last seen. Denies increased shortness of breath, increased sputum production, or productive cough. Reports good adherence to current inhaler regimen. No new concerns voiced today.

Medication List
1. Tiotropium inhaler daily
2. Lisinopril 10mg daily

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, in no acute distress.
Respiratory: CTAB, RRR, lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezing or rales.
CV: RRR, no murmurs.
Ext: No edema.

Assessment
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: Stable.

Plan
Continue current management plan for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Pt to continue current inhaler as prescribed. F/u in 3 months for routine clinic visit.

Electronically signed,
E. Castillo, DO
05/14/2026
explanations: A signed face-to-face visit with an acceptable provider (MD, DO, NP or PA) that assesses COPD supports J44.9 (HCC 280).

distractors.why: The visit is face to face, signed with credentials and addresses COPD: it supports J44.9.
